ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: about 2 cups; roasted rice flour gives a crispier result

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: about 1/4 cup; helps the batter adhere to the mould

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.notes: beaten; optional but helps the kokis release from the mould more easily

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 1 cup; add more gradually to reach correct batter thickness

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: for colour; start with less as colour deepens after frying

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: a small amount balances the batter; some traditional recipes omit it

ingredients.name: Oil for deep frying
ingredients.notes: coconut oil gives the best aroma; vegetable oil works

steps.instruction: Combine the rice flour, all-purpose flour, turmeric, sugar, and salt in a large bowl and mix well.
Beat the egg and add to the bowl along with the coconut milk, a little at a time, whisking until a smooth thick batter forms -- slightly thicker than pancake batter. Rest for 5-10 minutes.
Transfer some batter to a small deep bowl just wide enough for the kokis mould -- keeps the main batch from overheating.
Heat oil to 160-175C (320-350F). Season the kokis mould by submerging it in the hot oil for 2-3 minutes, then wipe dry.

Heat the mould in the oil for 15-20 seconds until very hot. Lift out and immediately dip into the batter coating about 3/4 of the mould depth -- do NOT fully submerge, as this makes the kokis impossible to remove.
Dip the coated mould back into the hot oil. Hold for 45-60 seconds until the batter sets and begins to separate from the mould. Shake gently or use a wooden skewer to ease the kokis off into the oil.
Fry until golden yellow-brown and crispy, about 1-2 more minutes. Remove and drain on paper towels. Repeat with remaining batter, stirring between batches.
Cool completely before serving or storing -- kokis achieve their final crispiness only after cooling. Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, 196flavors.com, tasty.co, maggi.lk, cuisinesofworld.com, lakpura.com, and dailylife.lk
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; very strong agreement on batter thickness, mould seasoning, and the 3/4-dip rule
notes: Kokis is believed to be of Dutch colonial origin (name from Dutch 'koekjes' meaning cookies), one of the few Sri Lankan festival foods with a directly traceable European origin. The kokis mould (kokis achchuwa) is essential -- Scandinavian rosette cookie moulds are nearly identical substitutes. The 3/4-dip rule is the single most consistently repeated critical technique across all sources reviewed.
